name: Brutalist
about: The Brutalist toolkit's look: a cream page, warm ink, EB Garamond for the argument, Lato Bold for labels, one terracotta spark. Mostly light slides, with dark ones as punctuation.
sources: brutalist.art DESIGN-PRINCIPLES.md (the palette, the type roles, restraint, light-to-dark balance)
The Brutalist-look HTML decks (cream paper, serif headlines, one warm accent)
bearbrown.co colour tokens (burnt orange #8B3A0F as the text-safe accent, the dark set)
rules: Warm, muted, restrained. No neon, no gradients, no glows, no drop shadows.

Terracotta (#D97757) is decoration only: it is under 3:1 on cream, so it never colours text or a thin line that must be read. Emphasis text is burnt orange (#8B3A0F) on cream and amber (#E8A020) on espresso.
The accent is an event. Use it at the one place the slide turns, never as a resting fill.
Serif for the argument (headlines, statements, body). Sans (Lato Bold) for labels, axes and sources. Mono for code and numbers. No other faces.
About four slides in five are light. A dark slide marks a shift: a statement, a turn in the argument.
No invented marks: no orbs, sparks, circuit boards, neural-net nodes, robot heads or holograms to mean AI.
Icons, when used, are simple line drawings. If the right one does not exist, ask for it; do not improvise a near miss.
